en: Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a makeshift bamboo incubator to keep premature babies warm in rural areas without electricity.
The Philippine Clean Air Act requires vehicles to undergo regular smoke emission tests to reduce harmful air pollution.
The Igorot people built Ifugao rice terraces with stone walls that prevent soil erosion and landslides during heavy rains.
PAGASA uses color-coded rainfall warning signals to help communities know exactly when to evacuate during dangerous typhoons.
Dr. Abelardo Aguilar discovered the antibiotic erythromycin from Iloilo soil samples, helping doctors treat dangerous bacterial infections worldwide.
Public health centers follow the Cold Chain system, using specialized refrigerators to keep government-provided vaccines scientifically effective and safe.
Traditional Filipino fish fermentation like bagoong requires strict salt ratios to prevent the growth of harmful foodborne bacteria.
Indigenous groups use overlapping anahaw leaves to build roofs that naturally shed heavy rain and protect against typhoons.
The Philippine Red Cross teaches children the Reach, Throw, Row water rescue steps to safely save drowning victims.
Jose Rizal used his medical training in Dapitan to safely drain swamps, reducing mosquito populations and preventing malaria.
Locals make Pahiyas kiping from rice dyed with natural plant extracts, creating a biodegradable, non-toxic alternative to plastic decorations.
The T'boli people extract natural dyes from local plants for t'nalak cloth, avoiding toxic synthetic chemicals that irritate skin.
